text:
ConocoPhillips gained 1.6% today, continuing a sharp recovery from its lows earlier this week. The stock has climbed nearly $6 (4.4%) over the past three days as oil prices stabilized—US crude is trading at $89.62 per barrel, a level that supports energy company earnings. The broader sector momentum has been positive: heating oil prices are up 59% from last winter, which benefits integrated oil companies with refining operations, and investor interest in energy stocks appears to have picked back up after the dip.

That said, the longer two-week decline of 7.6% reflects a genuine headwind: Russian crude output has rebounded sharply to 8.73 million barrels a day, pushing global oil markets back into surplus. Oversupply pressures can weigh on prices and refiner margins, which explains why the stock fell so much before this week's rebound. Today's move is a bounce on near-term stability, not a resolution of that underlying supply concern.
